//: Turbo runs tasks in strict env mode: a variable not named here is invisible to them. Connection strings and signing keys go in passThrough rather than globalEnv because they must not become part of a cache key — the build output does not depend on which database it will talk to or which secret it will sign with, and secrets do not belong in a hash. API_ORIGIN is the opposite case on both counts, which is why it is in `env` on the build task: apps/web bakes it into the /api rewrite in routes-manifest.json, so it genuinely changes the output and a cached build made against a different API would otherwise be restored over it. It also has to be named at all — framework inference allows NEXT_PUBLIC_* through for free, so the variable this one replaced never needed an entry here and this one does. Getting that wrong is a build that fails, not a site that misbehaves, which is the trade next.config.ts's guard is making. On the `openapi` task: it writes apps/api/openapi.json and compiles apps/api to do it, so it needs @moodnight/db built first exactly as `build` does — which is the whole reason it is a turbo task and not a plain pnpm script. It is uncached because the document it writes lives inside the package it writes it from, making the task its own cache input; it runs on demand, not on every build.
